tools.description:

    forecast (FHFA data back to 1975), estimated market rent, and neighborhood signals
    (schools, walkability, water quality, grocery/dining/outdoors proximity).

tools.name: affordability
tools.description:
Can this buyer afford this home? Returns the monthly PITI payment, front-end and
    back-end debt-to-income ratios (what a lender qualifies on), the income needed at a
    28% front-end ratio, estimated after-tax money left over each month, the cash cushion
    left after closing, and a plain Comfo

tools.name: compare_areas
tools.description:
Analyze and RANK 2-12 ZIPs or addresses side by side on the signals TerraVue has:
    home-price appreciation forecast (and how each compares to the national average),
    school rating, walkability, education level, and water quality. Returns the correct
    city name per ZIP, so locations are neve

tools.name: affordable_price
tools.description:
What's the most this buyer can afford? The reverse of `affordability` — 'what price
    can I afford?' instead of 'can I afford this specific home?'. Solves for the maximum
    home price under standard lender limits: a front-end DTI cap (default 28% = housing /
    gross income) and a back-end cap

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: affordability, affordable_price · Private data: request_capability · Public sink: affordability.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: affordability, affordable_price · Private data: request_capability · Public sink: affordability

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
